caldwell.h: Caldwell Twp. was formed 16 Feb 1798 from parts of Acquackanonk and Newark Twps., taking in the Horseneck Tract; it was renamed Fairfield Twp. on 6 Nov 1963. Livingston (1813), Fairmount (1862), Caldwell borough and Verona Twp. (now Cedar Grove) (1892), North Caldwell (1898), Essex Fells (1902) and West Caldwell (1904) were taken from it.

horseneck.h: The Horseneck Tract, west of First Watchung Mountain, was bought from the Lenape in 1702 under Newark’s proprietors; title disputes led to the Horseneck Riots of the 1740s. After the Revolution it became Caldwell Twp. (1798), the parent of Livingston, the Caldwells, Fairfield, Verona, Cedar Grove, Essex Fells and Roseland.

acquackanonk.h: Acquackanonk dates from the patent of 1693 and was incorporated 21 Feb 1798; it was in Essex Co. until Passaic Co. was made on 7 Feb 1837. Caldwell Twp. (part, 1798), Paterson Twp. (1831), Little Falls (1868) and Passaic (1869–71) were taken from it, and the rest became the City of Clifton on 26 Apr 1917.

newark.h: Newark Twp. was organized 31 Oct 1693 and once covered most of Essex Co.; Caldwell Twp. (part, 1798), Orange Twp. (1806) and Bloomfield Twp. (1812) were split from it, and Newark became a city in 1836.

bloomfield.h: Bloomfield Twp. was set off from Newark Twp. on 23 Mar 1812; Belleville (1839), Montclair (1868), Woodside (1869) and Glen Ridge (1895) were later taken from it, and Nutley came from Belleville in 1874.

livingston.h: Livingston Twp. was formed 5 Feb 1813 from Caldwell and Springfield Twps.; Fairmount (1862, now in West Orange) and Roseland (1908) were later set off from it.

orange.h: Orange Twp. was detached from Newark Twp. on 27 Nov 1806. Its land later became the separate Oranges, among them West Orange (1862–63), the only one listed as a present township on this map.

springfield.h: Springfield Twp. was formed 14 Apr 1794 from Newark and Elizabeth Twps.; New Providence Twp. (1809) and part of Livingston (1813) were taken from it. It was in Essex Co. until Union Co. was made in 1857.

newprov.h: New Providence Twp. was formed 8 Nov 1809 from Springfield Twp., in Essex Co. until Union Co. was made in 1857. Summit left in 1869 and New Providence borough in 1899; the rest was renamed Berkeley Heights on 6 Nov 1951.

westfield.h: Westfield Twp. was formed 27 Jan 1794 from Elizabeth Twp. and was in Essex Co. until Union Co. was made on 19 Mar 1857; it became the Town of Westfield in 1903.

hanover.h: Hanover was a precinct by 1720 and a township of the new Morris Co. on 25 Mar 1740, at first covering most of the county; Mendham (1749), Chatham (1806), Rockaway Twp. (part, 1844), Boonton (1866), Mountain Lakes (1924), Morris Plains (1926), East Hanover and Parsippany-Troy Hills (1928) were set off from it.

pequannock.h: Pequannock (Poquanock) became a township on 25 Mar 1740 and once spanned northern Morris Co.; Jefferson (1804), Rockaway Twp. (part, 1844), Boonton Twp. and Montville (1867), Butler (1901), Kinnelon and Lincoln Park (1922) and Riverdale (1923) were set off from it.

morris.h: Morris Twp. was formed 25 Mar 1740; Roxbury (1740), Mendham (part, 1749), Chatham (part, 1806), Morristown (1865, fully 1895) and Passaic Twp., now Long Hill (1866), were taken from it.

chatham.h: Chatham Twp. was formed 12 Feb 1806 from Hanover and Morris Twps.; Madison (1889), Chatham village and borough (1892, 1897) and Florham Park (1899) later left it.

mendham.h: Mendham Twp. was formed 29 Mar 1749 from Hanover, Morris and Roxbury Twps.; Randolph (1806) and Mendham Borough (1906) were taken from it.

chester.h: Chester Twp. was created 1 Apr 1799 from Roxbury and Washington Twps.; Chester Borough was taken from it on 3 Apr 1930.

saddle.h: Saddle River Twp. was created 20 Mar 1716 for Bergen Co. west of the Saddle River. Franklin (1771–72), Pompton (part, 1797), Manchester (1837), Glen Rock and Lodi (1894), Wallington (1895), Garfield (1898), East Paterson, now Elmwood Park (1916), and Fair Lawn (1924) were taken from it; the rest was renamed Saddle Brook in 1955.

franklin.h: Franklin Twp., Bergen Co., was split from Saddle River Twp. in 1771–72 and named for Gov. William Franklin; with Saddle River it gave land to Pompton Twp. in 1797. It is now Wyckoff and neighbouring towns.

newtown.h: Newtown (Newton) Twp. was the original township of Sussex Co.; Wantage (1754), Hardyston (1762), Frankford (1797), Byram (1798), Sparta and Lafayette (1845) were set off from it, and it was dissolved on 11 Apr 1864 into Andover, Hampton and Newton.

hardiston.h: Hardyston Twp. was set off from Newtown (Newton) Twp. by royal charter 25 Feb 1762; Vernon (1793), Sparta (1845), Franklin (1913) and Hamburg (1920) were later taken from it.

sparta.h: Sparta Twp. was formed 14 Apr 1845 from parts of Byram, Frankford, Hardyston and Newton Twps.

morristown.h: Morristown, first settled about 1715 as New Hanover, was the seat of Morris Co.; it became a town 6 Apr 1865 within Morris Twp. and fully separate in 1895.

orangetown.h: Orangetown is one of the original towns of Rockland Co., N.Y., which was set off from Orange Co. in 1798.

value.t: Helmer Kent Sr. plantation, Beaver Brook
items: Ratables: Helmer Kent 96 ac (1778), 106 ac (1780, 1785); Jacob Kint 106 ac (1790, "Helmer's son-same acres"); Widow Sarah 55, 44, 45 ac (1795–1797).
1776: Helmer Kent signs the Pequannock associators list. 1782: the bridge job is sold to Helmer Kent (Munsell). Helmer, Jacob and Sarah Kent are on the Rockaway church member list before 1808.
20 Feb 1781: "Helemigh & Sara" Kint marry at Pompton Plains; daughter Maria baptized 16 Apr 1781. 1 Jun 1786: "Hellemach & Sara Cook" Kent baptize Helmer at Parsippany.

8 Oct 1788: inventory of Helmer Kent dec'd by Aaron Bigelow & Abraham Kitchel, about £130 (cattle, horses, wagon, carpenter's tools, loom, a woman's and a man's saddle). He died intestate before this date.

7 Jul 1795: Jacob Kent, "a son and heir," petitions the Orphans' Court to divide his father's land. Children: Catharine, John, Sarah, Mary, Agnis, Helemar, Anna and Jacob, "six of whom are under age."

3 Nov 1795: division by Aaron Bigelow, James Kitchel & Silas Condict, "subject to the Right of Dower of the Widow." Lots run from Beaver Brook back to Benjamin Beach (1–4) and Abraham Kitchel (5–8): 1 Abner Beach, assignee of Jacob, 19.20 ac; 2 Helemer 14.54; 3 Anna 7.68; 4 Agnes 7.83; 5 Mary 8.09; 6 Sarah 8.34; 7 John 19.27; 8 Catharine Willis 10.5. About 95.45 ac in all. Lot 1 begins at a corner of Thomas Miles in Aaron Bigelow's line.

Lot 7, 7 Dec 1798, O 314: John & Elizabeth Kint to Benjamin Beach, £70; 19.27 ac from the 4th corner of Lot 6 in Beaver Brook, S37°30'E 14.80 ch to Samuel Nevill's survey, S52°30'W 14.78 ch to Lot 8, N37°30'W 11.30 ch, then along the brook.
1800, D 449: Sarah Kint (widow) to James Kitchell (workbook reads Mitchell); 8.84 ac, "old survey of Helmer Kent's plantation," by Lot No. 7, now Benjamin Beach's.
Lot 5, 24 Mar 1802, F 178: Mary Kent "as his Daughter" to Benjamin Beach, $90, by mark; 8.09 ac from a stake in Beaver Brook at a corner of Agnes Kent's lot.
1804, L 626: Helmer Kent dec'd to Rosanna Tiebow, widow; "Beaver Crook, tributary of Rockaway River, west of Baldwin Mountain."

Lot 3, 12 May 1807, O 187: Peter I. Lasher & Anna "alias Anna Kent" of Plattsburgh to Helmer Kent of South Hero, $100; 7 ac 68 rods, bounded NE by Helmer's share, SW by Agnes Palmer "alias Agnes Kent," NW by a brook. Calls Helmer Sr. "late of Rockaway."

Lot 2, 10 Jun 1807, M 509: Sarah Payne "late Sarah Kent" of South Hero & Helmer Kent to Benjamin Beach, $230; 14.54 ac from a mark in Beaver Brook at the NW corner of Lot 1, S39°E 22.50 ch, S52°30'W 6.70 ch to Lot 3, N37°30'W 23.75 ch, then along the brook.
Lot 4: Daniel Palmer & Agnes "alias Agnes Kent" from Benjamin Beach (compiler’s notes).
1810: James & Hannah Kitchel release dower in John's 19.27 ac (Lot 7) to Anthony Zeek, whose wife was a Rosanna.

caldwell.h: The Horseneck church was renamed Caldwell in 1787. Caldwell Twp. (now Fairfield Twp.) dates from 16 Feb 1798. The Borough of Caldwell was incorporated 10 Feb 1892 from Caldwell Twp.; West Caldwell was taken from it in 1904. It became the "Township of the Borough of Caldwell" in 1981 and a borough again in 1995.

west-caldwell.h: Incorporated as a borough 24 Feb 1904 from the Franklin and Westville settlements of Caldwell borough, which had been made from Caldwell Twp. in 1892. It became a township in 1981.

north-caldwell.h: Incorporated as a borough 31 Mar 1898 from Caldwell Twp. (now Fairfield Twp.). It became a township in 1982 and a borough again on 1 Jan 1992. Lindsley Road is in North Caldwell today.

fairfield.h: Formed 16 Feb 1798 as Caldwell Twp. from parts of Acquackanonk and Newark Twps.; renamed Fairfield Twp. on 6 Nov 1963. Parts later became Livingston (1813), Fairmount Twp. (1862), Caldwell borough and Verona Twp. (1892), North Caldwell (1898), Essex Fells (1902) and West Caldwell (1904).

verona.h: Part of Caldwell Twp. after the Revolution. Verona Twp. was formed from Caldwell Twp. in February 1892: it was incorporated by act of the Legislature on 7 Feb, and local accounts date the residents’ vote to separate to 17 Feb. The borough of Verona was made from part of it in 1907, and the old township was renamed Cedar Grove on 9 Apr 1908. Verona became a township in 1981.

cedar-grove.h: Incorporated as Verona Twp. by act of the Legislature on 7 Feb 1892, from part of Caldwell Twp. After Verona borough was made from part of it (referendum 30 Apr 1907), the township was renamed Cedar Grove on 9 Apr 1908.

essex-fells.h: Incorporated as a borough 31 Mar 1902 from Caldwell Twp. (now Fairfield Twp.). It became a township in 1981 and a borough again on 1 Jan 1992.

roseland.h: The community was first Centerville, renamed Roseland in 1874. Incorporated as a borough 10 Apr 1908 from Livingston Twp. Before that it was part of the Horseneck Tract.

livingston.h: Incorporated 5 Feb 1813 from Caldwell Twp. and Springfield Twp.; named for Gov. William Livingston. The land was part of the Horseneck Tract. The 1811 petition named the hamlets Centerville, Cheapside, Morehousetown, Northfield, Squiretown, Teedtown and Washington Place. Fairmount was set off in 1862 (now West Orange) and Roseland in 1908.

west-orange.h: Part of Newark Twp. until 27 Nov 1806, when the Oranges were detached as Orange Twp. Fairmount Twp. was incorporated 11 Mar 1862 and joined West Orange when it was incorporated as a township on 10 Apr 1863. West Orange became a town in 1900 and a township again in 1980.

montclair.h: Cranetown (the Crane home dates from 1694) was called West Bloomfield after the 1812 township was made; the name Montclair was adopted by 1860. Speertown was a Dutch farming community: Newark, then Bloomfield Twp. (1812), then Montclair. Montclair was formed as a township 15 Apr 1868 from Bloomfield, became a town on 24 Feb 1894 and a township again in 1980.

bloomfield.h: Incorporated 23 Mar 1812 from Newark Twp.; named for Gov. Joseph Bloomfield. Early neighbourhoods: Speertown, Stone House Plains (renamed Brookdale in 1873), Second River, Cranetown and Watsessing. Set off later: Belleville 1839, Montclair 1868, Woodside 1869, Glen Ridge 1895.

glen-ridge.h: Incorporated as a borough 13 Feb 1895 from Bloomfield Twp.

belleville.h: Also called Washington; the Second River settlement was renamed Belleville in 1797. Belleville Twp. was incorporated 8 Apr 1839 from Bloomfield; Franklin Twp. (Nutley) was set off 18 Feb 1874. A town in 1910 and a township since 1981.

nutley.h: Franklin Twp. was incorporated 18 Feb 1874 from Belleville Twp. and replaced by the Town of Nutley on 5 Mar 1902. The name comes from the Satterthwaite estate of 1844. A township since 1981.

newark.h: Settled in 1666 by Connecticut families under Robert Treat, who named it New Ark. Organized as a township 31 Oct 1693, incorporated under the Township Act of 1798 and reincorporated as a city 11 Apr 1836. Its western lands were split off: Orange Twp. 1806, Caldwell Twp. 1798, Bloomfield Twp. 1812. Deeds recorded only as "Newark Twp." are placed here.

clifton.h: Replaced Acquackanonk Twp. on 26 Apr 1917. Acquackanonk was formed 31 Oct 1693 (the Acquackanonk Patent), incorporated 21 Feb 1798 under the Township Act, and in Essex Co. until Passaic Co. was created on 7 Feb 1837. Set off from it: Caldwell 1798, Paterson Twp. 11 Apr 1831, Little Falls 1868, Passaic village 1869. Rifle Camp Park lies mostly in Woodland Park, with its eastern edge in Clifton.

little-falls.h: Incorporated as a township 2 Apr 1868 from Acquackanonk Twp. West Paterson (now Woodland Park) was taken from it in 1914.

woodland-park.h: Incorporated as the borough of West Paterson in 1914 from Little Falls Twp. (the pages give 25 Mar and 1 May); renamed Woodland Park effective 1 Jan 2009. Rifle Camp Park lies mostly in Woodland Park.

paterson.h: The Society for Establishing Useful Manufactures founded Paterson on 22 Nov 1791; a charter followed in 1792. Paterson Twp. was formed 11 Apr 1831 from Acquackanonk Twp. in Essex Co.; it joined the new Passaic Co. on 7 Feb 1837, became a city 14 Apr 1851 and was reincorporated 14 Mar 1861.

prospect-park.h: Incorporated 13 Mar 1901 from Manchester Twp., which no longer exists. Manchester Twp. was formed from Saddle River Twp. on 7 Feb 1837 and ended 8 Apr 1908.

haledon.h: Incorporated as a borough 8 Apr 1908 (referendum 21 May 1908) from the Oldham district of Manchester Twp.

west-milford.h: Formed 10 Mar 1834 from the westernmost half of Pompton Twp., then in Bergen Co. (a local history gives the act as 25 Feb 1834); it joined the new Passaic Co. on 7 Feb 1837. Newfoundland is a neighbourhood of West Milford; a small part of Newfoundland lies in Jefferson Twp., Morris Co., where the Pequannock River divides Passaic and Morris Counties.

saddle-brook.h: Saddle River Twp. was created 20 Mar 1716, covering Bergen Co. west of the Saddle River, and seceded from New Barbadoes in 1724. It took the name Saddle Brook on 8 Nov 1955. Set off from it: Glen Rock (14 Sep 1894), Lodi (22 Dec 1894), Wallington (2 Jan 1895), Garfield (15 Mar 1898), East Paterson, now Elmwood Park (18 Apr 1916) and Fair Lawn (6 Mar 1924).

elmwood-park.h: Dundee Lake residents voted on 18 Apr 1916 to leave Saddle River Twp.; the borough was incorporated as East Paterson and renamed Elmwood Park on 1 Jan 1973.

garfield.h: Incorporated as a borough 15 Mar 1898 from Saddle River Twp. and part of Wallington; became the City of Garfield 19 Apr 1917.

lodi.h: Incorporated as a borough 22 Dec 1894 from parts of Lodi Twp. (now South Hackensack) and Saddle River Twp.

fair-lawn.h: Incorporated as the borough of Fairlawn by an act of 6 Mar 1924 from Saddle River Twp.; spelled Fair Lawn from 1933. The early Dutch farm area was called Slooterdam, later Small Lots.

glen-rock.h: Formed 14 Sep 1894 from parts of Ridgewood Twp. and Saddle River Twp. (about 1,736 acres).

wallington.h: Created as a borough 2 Jan 1895 (referendum 31 Dec 1894) from parts of Bergen Twp. and Saddle River Twp.; sections went to Garfield in 1898.

westfield.h: Settled about 1720 as the West Fields of the Elizabethtown tract. Formed as a township 27 Jan 1794 from Elizabeth Twp. and incorporated under the Township Act 21 Feb 1798. In Essex Co. until Union Co. was made on 19 Mar 1857, so pre-1857 records are in Essex. Became a town 4 Mar 1903.

new-providence.h: First called Turkey or Turkey Town; renamed New Providence after a church balcony fell in 1759 without serious injury. Springfield Twp. (14 Apr 1794) included it; New Providence Twp. was formed 8 Nov 1809. Summit left in 1869 and New Providence became a borough in 1899.

berkeley-heights.h: The old New Providence Twp. was renamed Berkeley Heights on 6 Nov 1951, after New Providence had become a separate borough in 1899.

springfield-twp.h: Springfield Twp. was formed 14 Apr 1794 from parts of Newark and Elizabeth Twps., in Essex Co. until Union Co. was made in 1857. New Providence Twp. (1809) and part of Livingston (1813) were taken from it. The one Springfield row on this map is a 1795 tax ratable with no lot; it stays listed under Livingston, New Providence and Berkeley Heights.

sparta.h: Formed 14 Apr 1845 from parts of Byram, Frankford, Hardyston and Newton Twps.; Ogdensburg was set off 26 Feb 1914. The John P. Kent deed of 25 Aug 1845 (recorded 8 Oct 1845) names him of Sparta.

hardyston.h: Set off from Newton Twp. by royal charter 25 Feb 1762; named for Gov. Josiah Hardy and first spelled Hardiston. Incorporated 1798. Set off later: Vernon 1793, Sparta 1845, Franklin 1913, Hamburg 1920. The one Hardiston deed has no marker in the Essex or Morris views.

jefferson.h: Set off 11 Feb 1804 from Roxbury and Pequannock Twps. A small part of Newfoundland lies in Jefferson; the Pequannock River divides it from Passaic Co.

pequannock.h: A precinct called Poquanick by 1720; Poquanock Twp. on 25 Mar 1740, then the county's largest (about 176 sq mi); Pequanack in 1798. Set off: Jefferson 1804, Rockaway Twp. 1844, Boonton and Montville 1867, Butler 1901, Kinnelon and Lincoln Park 1922, Riverdale 1923. Pompton Plains is its main community.

montville.h: Incorporated 11 Apr 1867 from Pequannock Twp. Pine Brook is a section of Montville.

lincoln-park.h: Incorporated as a borough 11 Mar 1922 from Pequannock Twp.; reincorporated 26 Feb 1925.

rockaway-twp.h: Set off 8 Apr 1844 from Hanover and Pequannock. Before then the Rockaway village and Beaver Brook areas were in Hanover and Pequannock.

rockaway-borough.h: Incorporated as a borough 19 Jun 1894 from Rockaway Twp.; it annexed more of the township in 1908. Before 1844 the Rockaway village was in Hanover and Pequannock.

denville.h: Incorporated as a township 14 Apr 1913 from Rockaway Twp. Early forges and mills were built along Den Brook; the Franklin community in southern Denville grew up around them.

randolph.h: Set off from Mendham Twp. by an act of 13 Nov 1805, effective 1 Jan 1806. Named for Hartshorne Fitz-Randolph, who bought 1,000 acres at Mine Hill in 1753. Dover, Port Oram (now Wharton) and Mine Hill separated later.

hanover.h: Formed 1720 and incorporated 25 Mar 1740, at first covering most of Morris Co. Set off: Mendham 1749, Chatham 1806, Rockaway Twp. 1844, Boonton town 1866, Mountain Lakes 1924, Morris Plains 1926, East Hanover and Parsippany-Troy Hills 1928. Whippany is a community in Hanover Twp.

morristown.h: First settled about 1715 as New Hanover (also called West Hanover), and renamed for Gov. Lewis Morris; it became the seat of Morris Co., created 15 Mar 1739. Incorporated as a town 6 Apr 1865 while still part of Morris Twp.; fully separated from Morris Twp. in 1895.

chatham-twp.h: Incorporated 12 Feb 1806 from Hanover and Morris Twps.; named for William Pitt, Earl of Chatham. Madison (27 Dec 1889), Chatham village (1892; borough 1 Mar 1897) and Florham Park (20 Mar 1899) later left it.

chatham-borough.h: Settled about 1710 and known as John Day’s Bridge; renamed Chatham in 1773 for William Pitt, Earl of Chatham. Incorporated as a village 19 Aug 1892 within Chatham Twp. and reincorporated as a borough 1 Mar 1897, fully independent of the township.

morris-twp.h: Formed 25 Mar 1740. Set off: Roxbury 24 Dec 1740, Mendham 1749, Chatham 1806, Morristown 1865 (fully independent 1895), Passaic Twp. (now Long Hill) 1866. The one place on this map recorded as in Morris Twp. (M, north side of Long Hill) lies in present Long Hill or Harding, so its deeds are listed there.

long-hill.h: Incorporated as Passaic Twp. 23 Mar 1866 from Morris Twp.; part became Harding Twp. on 1 Sep 1922. Renamed Long Hill Twp. after a vote on 3 Nov 1992, to avoid confusion with the City of Passaic.

harding.h: Incorporated 1 Sep 1922 from Passaic Twp. (now Long Hill Twp.), after a referendum on 9 May 1922; named for Pres. Warren G. Harding. New Vernon and part of Green Village lie in it.

chester-twp.h: Created 1 Apr 1799 from Roxbury and Washington Twps., following a local referendum; named for Chester(shire), England. Chester Borough was taken from it on 3 Apr 1930.

chester-borough.h: The village of Chester, earlier called Black River, was settled about 1713 by families from Long Island. It was incorporated as a borough 3 Apr 1930 from Chester Twp., which surrounds it.

mendham-twp.h: Formed 29 Mar 1749 from Hanover, Morris and Roxbury Twps.; incorporated under the Township Act 21 Feb 1798. Randolph was taken from it on 1 Jan 1806 and Mendham Borough on 15 May 1906. Roxiticus is in Mendham.

mendham-borough.h: Incorporated as a borough 15 May 1906 from Mendham Twp. The village grew around the Black Horse Tavern (about 1742).
